newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday mainly due to a continued technical correction after sharp gains early this week, traders said.
But the annual rate for the most active seven-day contract ended higher at 10.30 percent from 9.98 on Wednesday due to active and rising domestic A share markets, they said.
Turnover surged to 11.44 million lots from 6.17 million lots. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The most active contract was encouraged by the rise of the A share markets both in Shanghai and Shenzhen," a trader said.
Analysts said repo rates were likely to move around the current high levels in the next few days if the A share markets continued to rise.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday and traders said they hit support levels on Wednesday after having fallen for weeks.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in 2006 closed up at 120.90 yuan from 103.40.
Combined volume on the eight-contract market rose to 2.23 million lots from 929,328.
Traders said the contracts would continue to rebound in the next few days. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
